_comment: The one hand-written source for the settings documentation. docs/tools/generate_settings_reference.py turns it, with what the code itself says (defaults, where each setting is read), into .env.example and docs/public/reference/configuration.html. verify/v154_settings_documented.py fails when this file, the code and those two outputs disagree.

groups.title: Folders and files on this machine
groups.intro: Where the platform keeps its data, its scratch work and its logs. Most of these hang off one folder, MUNITAS_DATA, so that moving the data folder moves everything with it.

groups.title: Keys and secrets
groups.intro: Values that must be kept private. Each has a development value so that a laptop starts without any setup. A development value is published in this repository, so it must be replaced in any shared or production deployment. MUNITAS_ENV can enforce that.

groups.title: Production safety
groups.intro: A switch that makes the platform refuse to run on published secrets.

groups.title: Object storage
groups.intro: Where files are stored, and how the platform reaches the storage engine.

groups.title: Cloudflare R2 (optional)
groups.intro: R2 is an optional second storage backend. Leave every R2 setting empty on an installation that only uses the built-in storage: a dataset then cannot be sealed against R2, and the refusal says why. The four credential values must come from one and the same R2 API token, created under R2, API, Manage API tokens, with Admin Read and Write permission. Cloudflare shows the token value once, when it is created. The access key id is the token's id, and the secret access key is a SHA-256 hash of its value. Mixing values from two tokens produces a credential that signs storage requests as one identity and Cloudflare requests as another, and that fails in a way that reads like a permissions problem.

groups.title: Services the platform talks to
groups.intro: The addresses of the other services. Inside the Compose network they are service names and need no change. The host worker reaches the same services on the ports published on this machine.

groups.title: Containers, networks and work queues
groups.intro: The names the worker uses for the Docker networks, the image and the work queue of the containers it starts. They change only if the Compose project is renamed.

groups.title: How long access lasts
groups.intro: The lifetimes of the credentials and keys the platform hands out. Short lifetimes are the point: access ends by itself.

groups.title: Closing an organisation and legal holds
groups.intro: An organisation is closed in two waiting periods and then deleted unless a legal hold stands. Each organisation takes its dates from these settings when its closing starts, so changing them never moves a countdown that is already running.

groups.title: Legal export
groups.intro: A legal export is an encrypted, signed package kept in a bucket of its own and deleted after a set number of days.

groups.title: Writing a version's rows as a table
groups.intro: A caller who names a records file is asking for a table. By default a version is then not sealed without one when the table cannot be written for a reason about the data or a fault in writing it: the seal is refused with the reason, and nothing is left behind. A caller that would rather keep the files without a table says so for one seal. A table that is not written because the platform was told not to, because the files are on R2, or because the file is too large never blocks a seal. The records file comes in one of three shapes, chosen by its name: a JSON list (.json), one JSON row per line (.ndjson or .jsonl) or a Parquet file (.parquet). A JSON list is read whole and takes about six times its size in memory, so its limit is small. The other two are read in batches, so their memory use does not depend on the file, and their limit is on time.

groups.title: Bringing in a table in parts
groups.intro: A person sends a large file in parts through the platform, each of which can be sent again, and the file becomes a table that a worker writes. These limits keep a few people from slowing everybody else down. An organisation's own limits (its largest file, how many tables are written at once, how much it may keep waiting and bring in a day) are limits, which the organisation can lower.

groups.title: Large tables (table jobs)
groups.intro: A table that is large is written by a worker, in a job, and not while a request waits. A seal that names a records file bigger than the inline limit becomes a job. A job is not tied to a request's deadline, so its size limit is far higher than the request limit, and its time limit is the lifetime of its key. The limits a job works within are sent to the worker by the platform, so they are set here and nowhere else.

groups.title: De-identification models and pipeline runs
groups.intro: The speech and detection models the worker loads, and the organisation that pipeline runs started from this machine belong to.

groups.title: Logging
groups.intro: What the control plane writes to its log output. It logs identifiers and numbers, never contents.

groups.title: Set by the platform for the containers it starts
groups.intro: The platform passes these to short-lived containers (a query runner, a file staging step, a custom pipeline step) when it starts them. They are listed so that nothing in the environment is unexplained. Do not set them yourself.

settings.name: MUNITAS_DATA
settings.meaning: The one folder that holds the platform's data on this machine: stored files, the synthetic sample files, downloaded models, scratch work and logs. Use an absolute path with room for several gigabytes of model downloads. Nothing starts without it. Docker Compose and the start script read it from .env, and the start script passes it on to the workers.

settings.name: MUNITAS_WORK
settings.meaning: The scratch folder a worker uses while it runs a pipeline. By default it is the folder work inside MUNITAS_DATA. It must be an absolute path that is valid on the operating system the worker runs on, and the worker creates it when it is missing.

settings.name: MUNITAS_CORPUS
settings.meaning: The folder of synthetic sample files that practice runs and verification runs read. By default it is the folder synthetic inside MUNITAS_DATA. It is only read, never changed, so it must already exist.

settings.name: MUNITAS_LOG_DIR
settings.meaning: The folder each worker writes its log file into. By default it is the folder logs inside MUNITAS_DATA. A log rolls over at 10 MB and five old files are kept, so logs cannot fill the disk. It must be an absolute path.

settings.name: MUNITAS_ALERTS_FILE
settings.meaning: The file that alerts are written to: one line of JSON per alert, in one file for every category of alert, each line carrying its category. Inside the API container the path is under /logs, which is the logs folder of MUNITAS_DATA, so by default the file is MUNITAS_DATA/logs/alerts.jsonl on this machine. It rolls over at 10 MB and five old files are kept. An empty value switches the file off, and alerts are then recorded only in the log output and by the part of the platform that raised them.

settings.name: MUNITAS_KEY_SERVICE_MASTER_FILE
settings.meaning: The file that holds the master key of the key service, which keeps each person's key. It is read from a mounted file and never from the environment or the database. The API starts without it, and only the routes that lock a person's data need it. The start script creates the file under infra/secrets.

settings.name: MUNITAS_API_CA_CERT
settings.meaning: A self-signed certificate that the worker trusts in addition to the operating system's own list, for use when MUNITAS_API points at a local HTTPS listener. Only the worker trusts it. Nothing is installed in the operating system's trust store. It is ignored when the file does not exist.

settings.name: MUNITAS_HOST_WORK_DIR
settings.meaning: Only needed for the optional quickstart worker that runs inside Docker Compose (docker compose --profile quickstart up). The absolute path, on this machine, of the folder that worker uses for scratch work. It is not a path inside a container. The folder is created when it is missing. When it is wrong or unset, the quickstart worker refuses to start instead of writing files somewhere that would confuse whatever looks for them later.

settings.name: MUNITAS_STORAGE_PATH
settings.meaning: The folder on the host where the storage engine keeps its volume files. It is shown on the Storage housekeeping page so that an administrator can see where an organisation's files really are. Nothing reads or writes through it. Docker Compose sets it from MUNITAS_DATA.

settings.name: MUNITAS_PG_DSN
settings.meaning: The connection string for the platform's database, with the user and password in it. The API requires it, and Docker Compose builds it from MUNITAS_PG_USER and MUNITAS_PG_PASSWORD. The verification checks, when run from this machine, need it set to the database's published port. The worker uses the local database on its published port when it is not set.

settings.name: MUNITAS_PG_USER
settings.meaning: The database user. The database container creates it and the API connects as it.

settings.name: MUNITAS_PG_PASSWORD
settings.meaning: The password of the database user. A development value is used when it is not set.

settings.name: MUNITAS_MASTER_KEY
settings.meaning: The master key that wraps the platform's data keys. The API will not start without it. Docker Compose supplies a development value when none is set.

settings.name: MUNITAS_SIGNING_KEY
settings.meaning: The key that signs the manifest of a legal export, so that whoever receives the package can verify it. The public half is served at /legal-exports/signing-key. Keep it like the master key.

settings.name: MUNITAS_WORKER_TOKEN
settings.meaning: A secret shared by the API and the host worker, checked on the one endpoint that serves an agent version's code to the worker. When it is unset on the API, that endpoint refuses every request, and the API still starts. Set the same value on both sides.

settings.name: MUNITAS_OPA_TOKEN
settings.meaning: A secret shared by the API and the policy engine. The policy engine answers only a caller that presents it, and then only for decisions, so no other container or process on the machine can read its policies or replace one. The development value is published in this repository, so a production start refuses it.
settings.shown: A development value, published in this repository

settings.name: MUNITAS_S3_ADMIN_KEY
settings.meaning: The access key of the storage administrator identity, which creates buckets.

settings.name: MUNITAS_S3_ADMIN_SECRET
settings.meaning: The secret of the storage administrator identity. Every storage key the platform hands out, one per organisation, per job and per catalog session, is derived from this secret, so anybody who has read the published development value could compute them all. Replace it in any shared deployment.

settings.name: MUNITAS_S3_PIPELINE_KEY
settings.meaning: The access key of the standing storage identity of the pipeline action role. Each role that holds a storage key has one pair, and the platform compiles them into the storage permissions document. Leave it empty to use the development value.

settings.name: MUNITAS_S3_PIPELINE_SECRET
settings.meaning: The secret of the standing storage identity of the pipeline action role. Leave it empty to use the development value; set your own in any shared deployment.

settings.name: MUNITAS_S3_TRAINING_JOB_KEY
settings.meaning: The access key of the standing storage identity of the training job role. Each role that holds a storage key has one pair, and the platform compiles them into the storage permissions document. Leave it empty to use the development value.

settings.name: MUNITAS_S3_TRAINING_JOB_SECRET
settings.meaning: The secret of the standing storage identity of the training job role. Leave it empty to use the development value; set your own in any shared deployment.

settings.name: MUNITAS_S3_ANNOTATION_TOOL_KEY
settings.meaning: The access key of the standing storage identity of the annotation tool role. Each role that holds a storage key has one pair, and the platform compiles them into the storage permissions document. Leave it empty to use the development value.

settings.name: MUNITAS_S3_ANNOTATION_TOOL_SECRET
settings.meaning: The secret of the standing storage identity of the annotation tool role. Leave it empty to use the development value; set your own in any shared deployment.

settings.name: MUNITAS_S3_NOTEBOOK_EXPLORE_KEY
settings.meaning: The access key of the standing storage identity of the researcher notebook role. Each role that holds a storage key has one pair, and the platform compiles them into the storage permissions document. Leave it empty to use the development value.

settings.name: MUNITAS_S3_NOTEBOOK_EXPLORE_SECRET
settings.meaning: The secret of the standing storage identity of the researcher notebook role. Leave it empty to use the development value; set your own in any shared deployment.

settings.name: MUNITAS_S3_AGENT_RUNTIME_KEY
settings.meaning: The access key of the standing storage identity of the agent runtime role. Each role that holds a storage key has one pair, and the platform compiles them into the storage permissions document. Leave it empty to use the development value.

settings.name: MUNITAS_S3_AGENT_RUNTIME_SECRET
settings.meaning: The secret of the standing storage identity of the agent runtime role. Leave it empty to use the development value; set your own in any shared deployment.

settings.name: MUNITAS_ENV
settings.meaning: Set it to production and the platform refuses to start while the storage administrator secret or the worker token still holds the value published in this repository. The refusal names the settings at fault and never prints their values. Any other value, or none, is a development start.

settings.name: MUNITAS_S3_ENDPOINT
settings.meaning: The address the platform uses to reach object storage. Inside the Compose network it is http://seaweedfs:8333. The host worker and the scripts use the published port on localhost instead.
settings.shown: http://seaweedfs:8333 for the API, http://localhost:<storage port> for the worker

settings.name: MUNITAS_PUBLIC_S3_ENDPOINT
settings.meaning: The storage address that a person's own tool (DuckDB or PyIceberg, for example) can reach from their machine. The table catalog puts it in the configuration it hands out. The API itself reaches storage at MUNITAS_S3_ENDPOINT, which only exists inside the Compose network.

settings.name: MUNITAS_FILER_URL
settings.meaning: The address of the storage engine's filer, where the permissions document is kept. It is reached inside the Compose network and is never published.

settings.name: MUNITAS_MASTER_URL
settings.meaning: The address of the storage engine's master, which the platform asks for volume status and tells to grow volumes.

settings.name: MUNITAS_STORAGE_VOLUMES_PER_TENANT
settings.meaning: How many storage volumes an organisation's bucket is given when it first writes. A volume is a large file that many stored objects are appended into, up to 1 GB, and volumes are never shared between organisations, so this is paid per organisation and not per byte. One is right for many small organisations. An organisation that fills its volume is given another automatically, so a value that is too low costs a brief pause, while a value that is too high can run the machine out of volumes. An organisation expected to be large says so when it is onboarded, and that wins over this setting.

settings.name: MUNITAS_R2_ACCOUNT_ID
settings.meaning: The Cloudflare account id.

settings.name: MUNITAS_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID
settings.meaning: The id of the R2 API token. It is the access key of the S3 side.

settings.name: MUNITAS_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
settings.meaning: The SHA-256 hash of the R2 API token's value, which is the secret of the S3 side. Verification checks that this pair really belongs to the token below, so a mismatched paste is caught by name.

settings.name: MUNITAS_R2_API_TOKEN
settings.meaning: The R2 API token itself. Cloudflare's own REST API (creating a bucket, minting a scoped token, issuing a temporary credential) authenticates with this value as a bearer, while the S3 protocol uses the id and the hash above. The hash is one way, so this value has to be carried separately.

settings.name: MUNITAS_OPA_URL
settings.meaning: The address of the policy engine, which decides every request.

settings.name: MUNITAS_OPA_POLICY_SOURCE
settings.meaning: How the policy engine gets its policy. folder: it reads the policy folder and reloads when a file changes, which is quickest while you are changing the rules; a change that does not compile is logged and the last good policy keeps answering. bundle: it fetches a signed package that publish-policy.ps1 has tested, built and put in storage, and a package that is unsigned, signed by another key, altered or otherwise does not load is refused and leaves the last good one in place. A production start (MUNITAS_ENV=production) requires bundle. Only the start scripts read it; anything other than folder or bundle is refused by name.

settings.name: MUNITAS_MLFLOW_URL
settings.meaning: The address of the score store that a de-identification run writes its score card to. The API only asks whether it is up, before such a run starts.
settings.shown: http://mlflow:5000 for the API, http://localhost:<score store port> for the worker

settings.name: MUNITAS_KRATOS_PUBLIC_URL
settings.meaning: The public address of the sign-in service, used to verify a person's session. The API starts before the sign-in service is ready, and without it, so this is not required at start-up.

settings.name: MUNITAS_KRATOS_ADMIN_URL
settings.meaning: The admin address of the sign-in service. Only a purge uses it, to remove the sign-in accounts of the organisation it deletes, and nothing else.

settings.name: MUNITAS_TEMPORAL_ADDRESS
settings.meaning: The address of the workflow engine, as host and port.
settings.shown: temporal:7233 inside the Compose network, localhost:<workflow engine port> for the worker

settings.name: MUNITAS_LABEL_STUDIO_URL
settings.meaning: The address of the annotation tool, as the worker reaches it.

settings.name: MUNITAS_API
settings.meaning: The address of the control plane (the API), as the worker and the table worker reach it. The worker refuses to start when this points off the machine over plain HTTP, because the same traffic carries a person's HuggingFace token and the worker token. Use an https address for a real deployment.
settings.shown: http://localhost:<API port> for the worker, http://munitas-api:8000 for the table worker

settings.name: MUNITAS_SANDBOX_API
settings.meaning: Where a sandboxed agent run reaches the control plane from inside its own network. It is a service name, resolved from inside the sandbox container.

settings.name: MUNITAS_CONSOLE_ORIGINS
settings.meaning: The origins that may call the API from a browser, as a comma separated list. They are listed and never replaced by a wildcard, because a wildcard would let any page the operator happens to visit drive the control plane. Compose builds the value from the console's ports. The API must also stay bound to localhost.

settings.name: MUNITAS_AGENTNET
settings.meaning: The Docker network that a sandboxed agent run's own container joins. It is internal, with no route out.

settings.name: MUNITAS_STEPNET
settings.meaning: The only Docker network that a custom pipeline step's container joins when it reads files. It is internal, with no route to the internet. The one thing on it is a small gateway that forwards the platform's step routes and nothing else.

settings.name: MUNITAS_DATA_NETWORK
settings.meaning: The Docker network that the file staging container reaches storage on. Never the agent network.

settings.name: MUNITAS_SANDBOX_TASK_QUEUE
settings.meaning: The work queue that the Docker dependent half of agent runs is routed to, so that a second worker inside the Linux distribution, next to the Docker socket, can serve just that.

settings.name: MUNITAS_DERIVE_IMAGE
settings.meaning: The image that the three containers of a derivation (a query that makes a new dataset) run from.

settings.name: MUNITAS_CREDENTIAL_TTL_MINUTES
settings.meaning: How long a minted credential lasts. It is short, because the whole argument for leases is that access expires on its own and does not wait for somebody to remember.

settings.name: MUNITAS_CATALOG_TOKEN_MAX_HOURS
settings.meaning: The longest a table catalog token may live. A token carries a person's purpose and nothing else, and each table it opens is still decided on its own.

settings.name: MUNITAS_CATALOG_KEY_SECONDS
settings.meaning: The longest a storage key handed out by the table catalog lasts. A key is one of a rolling series, so it lives between half of this and all of it. Values below 40 are raised to 40, because a key could otherwise be refused before the document that holds it is written.

settings.name: MUNITAS_WRITE_GRANT_ACTIVE_SECONDS
settings.meaning: How long a write grant keeps its key after its task last asked for it. A task asks again at every step and every retry, so this has to outlast the longest gap between two asks, and not the length of a whole run.

settings.name: MUNITAS_API_SLOW_REQUEST_SECONDS
settings.meaning: A request to the platform that takes this long or longer is written to the log as a warning that names the route and the time it took, so a slow screen can be traced to the request behind it. Use 0 to switch the warning off.

settings.name: MUNITAS_RETIRING_DAYS
settings.meaning: The first waiting period of closing an organisation. Its people can still read and may cancel the closing.

settings.name: MUNITAS_CLOSING_DAYS
settings.meaning: The second waiting period. Its people can do nothing, and a platform administrator may place a legal hold. When both periods end and no hold stands, everything inside the organisation is deleted.

settings.name: MUNITAS_HOLD_APPROVAL_DAYS
settings.meaning: How long a proposed legal hold waits for a second administrator before it lapses and stops standing in the way of the deletion.

settings.name: MUNITAS_HOLD_REVIEW_DAYS
settings.meaning: How long an approved legal hold runs before somebody has to look at it again.

settings.name: MUNITAS_AUDIT_RETENTION_YEARS
settings.meaning: How many years the audit rows of a deleted organisation (who read what) are kept, after which they are removed. Seven is the retention period the platform was asked to meet.

settings.name: MUNITAS_LIFECYCLE_SWEEP_SECONDS
settings.meaning: How often the platform looks for organisations whose time is up. 0 turns the timer off, and the sweep can still be run by hand. A verification run uses 0 so that a deletion only happens when it asks for one.

settings.name: MUNITAS_DEVELOPMENT_SWEEP_SECONDS
settings.meaning: How often development samples that have run out are ended and what was made from them is deleted. 0 turns the timer off.

settings.name: MUNITAS_LEGAL_EXPORT_BUCKET
settings.meaning: The bucket that legal export packages are kept in.

settings.name: MUNITAS_LEGAL_EXPORT_KEEP_DAYS
settings.meaning: How long a package is kept before it is deleted.

settings.name: MUNITAS_LEGAL_EXPORT_LINK_DAYS
settings.meaning: How long the download link of a package works.

settings.name: MUNITAS_LEGAL_EXPORT_LINK_USES
settings.meaning: How many times the download link of a package may be used.

settings.name: MUNITAS_LEGAL_EXPORT_MAX_BYTES
settings.meaning: The most a package may hold. A package is built on local disk, so this is a safety limit and not a design goal.

settings.name: MUNITAS_ICEBERG_PROJECTION
settings.meaning: Set it to off to skip writing tables entirely, so that a deployment that has not given the API enough memory for pyarrow can still seal versions as files.

settings.name: MUNITAS_ICEBERG_FAIL_CLOSED
settings.meaning: By default a version whose caller asked for a table is not sealed when the table cannot be written. Set it to off to seal the files anyway and record the reason.

settings.name: MUNITAS_ICEBERG_MAX_BYTES
settings.meaning: The largest JSON list file that is turned into a table while a request waits. Measured here, a JSON list takes about six times its size in memory.

settings.name: MUNITAS_ICEBERG_STREAM_MAX_BYTES
settings.meaning: The largest newline delimited JSON or Parquet file that is turned into a table while a request waits. Such files are read in batches, so their limit is on time, at about 10 MB a second for JSON rows.

settings.name: MUNITAS_ICEBERG_BATCH_ROWS
settings.meaning: How many rows are read at a time from a newline delimited JSON or Parquet file.

settings.name: MUNITAS_ICEBERG_MAX_ROW_BYTES
settings.meaning: The longest one line of newline delimited JSON may be, so that a file with no line breaks cannot fill memory.

settings.name: MUNITAS_ICEBERG_PARQUET_MAX_ROW_GROUP_BYTES
settings.meaning: A Parquet file is read one row group at a time. A file whose row groups are larger than this when uncompressed, as its own footer states, is refused, because that is the amount that has to be held at once.

settings.name: MUNITAS_ICEBERG_PARQUET_THRIFT_STRING_BYTES
settings.meaning: The longest string the Parquet footer may declare. The footer is read with limits, because a hostile footer is the usual way to make a reader allocate without bound.

settings.name: MUNITAS_ICEBERG_PARQUET_THRIFT_CONTAINER_ITEMS
settings.meaning: The most items one list in the Parquet footer may declare, for the same reason.

settings.name: MUNITAS_ICEBERG_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
settings.meaning: How long writing one table may take before it is given up. Every call that leaves the process needs a deadline.

settings.name: MUNITAS_ICEBERG_ROW_GROUP_ROWS
settings.meaning: How many rows go in one Parquet row group when a table is written. 0 leaves the library's own default of about a million. A reader fetches one row group at a time, so a smaller group spreads a long scan over more, separate storage requests.
settings.shown: 0, which leaves the library's own default of about a million rows

settings.name: MUNITAS_ICEBERG_FILE_BYTES
settings.meaning: The number of bytes after which a table's rows continue in a new data file. 0 means the platform's own default of 64 MB. The library counts uncompressed bytes held in memory and holds that much before it writes a file, so 64 MB keeps a large write within a bounded share of memory, and the files come out several times smaller after compression. A tool that reads one file at a time opens each with the key it held when it started, so many small files spread a long read over many separate key checks.
settings.shown: 0, which means the platform's own default of 64 MiB

settings.name: MUNITAS_TABLE_JOBS
settings.meaning: Set it to off to switch table jobs off. Every table is then written inside the request, within the size limits that apply to a request, and a caller who asks for a table to be written in the background is refused.

settings.name: MUNITAS_TABLE_JOB_INLINE_BYTES
settings.meaning: A seal that names a records file bigger than this becomes a job. A caller can also ask for a job, or refuse one.

settings.name: MUNITAS_TABLE_JOB_MAX_BYTES
settings.meaning: The largest records file a job accepts.

settings.name: MUNITAS_TABLE_JOB_TTL_SECONDS
settings.meaning: How long a job's storage key lives, which is the time limit of the job.

settings.name: MUNITAS_TABLE_JOB_STALL_SECONDS
settings.meaning: A job that has waited this long for a worker is reported on the Storage housekeeping page as stalled.

settings.name: MUNITAS_TABLE_JOB_DISPATCH_SECONDS
settings.meaning: How often the platform hands waiting jobs to workers.

settings.name: MUNITAS_TABLE_TENANT
settings.meaning: Set on a dedicated table worker: the one organisation it serves, on that organisation's own line of work, and it refuses a job of any other. Left out, the worker serves the shared pool.

settings.name: MUNITAS_TABLE_DEDICATED
settings.meaning: Set by Docker Compose on a dedicated table worker. A dedicated worker that is not told which organisation it serves refuses to start.

settings.name: MUNITAS_TABLE_WORKER_TENANT
settings.meaning: The organisation that the dedicated table worker in Docker Compose serves. It is passed to the worker as MUNITAS_TABLE_TENANT.

settings.name: MUNITAS_WHISPER_MODEL
settings.meaning: The speech to text model. Eight gigabytes of video memory is the binding constraint, so models load and unload in sequence and do not stay resident.

settings.name: MUNITAS_WHISPER_COMPUTE
settings.meaning: The numeric precision of the speech model. The default keeps the large model to roughly 3 to 4 GB of video memory.

settings.name: MUNITAS_WHISPER_DEVICE
settings.meaning: The device the speech model runs on. The devices registered today are cuda and cpu.

settings.name: MUNITAS_GLINER_MODEL
settings.meaning: The GLiNER model, one of the detectors that finds identifying detail in text.

settings.name: MUNITAS_SPACY_MODEL
settings.meaning: The spaCy language model, one of the detectors that finds names and places in text.

settings.name: MUNITAS_TENANT
settings.meaning: The organisation that pipeline runs started from this machine belong to. They are verification runs, so by default they land in a test organisation named canary and not beside an example organisation. Change it to point the worker at a real organisation.

settings.name: MUNITAS_LOG_LEVEL
settings.meaning: The level of the control plane's log: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR or CRITICAL. The platform writes no debug lines, so DEBUG shows nothing more than INFO. That is deliberate: a debug level that can be switched on in production invites logging more than belongs there.

settings.name: MUNITAS_DERIVE_DATA
settings.meaning: The folder, inside the query runner's container, that holds one folder per input, named by its alias.

settings.name: MUNITAS_DERIVE_OUT
settings.meaning: The folder, inside the query runner's container, that the result is written into.

settings.name: MUNITAS_DERIVE_JOB
settings.meaning: The job file inside the query runner's container: the query, the inputs, the primary key and the fields.

settings.name: MUNITAS_DERIVE_MAX_ROWS
settings.meaning: The most rows the result of a query may have. A query whose result has more fails.

settings.name: MUNITAS_DERIVE_MAX_BYTES
settings.meaning: The most bytes the result of a query may take up. A query whose result is larger fails.

settings.name: MUNITAS_PUT_FILE
settings.meaning: The file in the result folder that the staging container uploads. It is records.json when not set.

settings.name: MUNITAS_PUT_KEY
settings.meaning: The object the staging container writes the result to.

settings.name: MUNITAS_S3_ACCESS_KEY
settings.meaning: The access key a staging container is given for one job. It reaches that container and nowhere else.

settings.name: MUNITAS_S3_SECRET_KEY
settings.meaning: The secret of the key above.

settings.name: MUNITAS_S3_SESSION_TOKEN
settings.meaning: The session token of the key above, when the key is a temporary one.

settings.name: MUNITAS_S3_BUCKET
settings.meaning: The bucket a staging container reads from or writes to.

settings.name: MUNITAS_STEP_API
settings.meaning: The address a custom pipeline step reaches the step gateway at, from inside its own network.

settings.name: MUNITAS_STEP_PASS
settings.meaning: The pass that identifies one step to the gateway. It holds for that one step and nothing else.

settings.name: MUNITAS_HYDRA_ADMIN_URL
settings.meaning: The admin address of the notebook sign-in service, which issues, renews and ends the short-lived pass a notebook signs in with. It stays private to the platform's own services and is never published on this machine.

settings.name: MUNITAS_HYDRA_PUBLIC_URL
settings.meaning: The address the API itself uses to reach the notebook sign-in service to start a sign-in, check its code and renew a pass. It is not the address a person's browser is sent to; that is set by the sign-in service itself, from the port in config.json.

settings.name: MUNITAS_NOTEBOOK_CLIENT_ID
settings.meaning: The name every notebook signs in under at the notebook sign-in service. The platform creates it there the first time a notebook signs in. Change it only if another client of that service already uses the default.

settings.name: MUNITAS_NOTEBOOK_SIGN_IN_HOURS
settings.meaning: The longest a notebook stays signed in as a person, in hours, however often it renews its pass. The person can end it sooner. Docker Compose gives the same value to the sign-in service, so the platform and the service cannot disagree. A change applies to sign-ins approved after it.

settings.name: MUNITAS_NOTEBOOK_ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES
settings.meaning: How long a notebook's pass lasts before the notebook renews it, in minutes. Short on purpose: a copied pass stops working soon, and the renewal is automatic. Read by Docker Compose and given to the sign-in service.

settings.name: MUNITAS_HYDRA_SYSTEM_SECRET
settings.meaning: The secret the notebook sign-in service uses to protect what it stores. At least 16 characters. Docker Compose supplies a development value when none is set; a real deployment must set its own and keep it out of the repository. Never put the value in documentation.

settings.name: MUNITAS_TABLE_UPLOAD_LIFE_HOURS
settings.meaning: How long an upload that has not been finished stays open, and so how long it holds a version number. After this the parts already sent are thrown away.

settings.name: MUNITAS_TABLE_UPLOAD_OPEN_PER_PERSON
settings.meaning: How many uploads one person may have open at once, meaning started and not yet finished or cancelled.

settings.name: MUNITAS_TABLE_LOCK_BATCH_ROWS
settings.meaning: How many rows of a table about people a table worker sends to the platform to be locked in one call. Larger is faster until one call is slow enough for everybody else to notice.

settings.name: MUNITAS_TABLE_LOCK_MAX_ROWS
settings.meaning: The most rows the platform accepts to lock in one call from a table worker. A call with more is refused.

settings.name: MUNITAS_TABLE_UPLOAD_PER_HOUR
settings.meaning: How many uploads one person may start in an hour.

settings.name: MUNITAS_TABLE_UPLOAD_REFUSED_PER_HOUR
settings.meaning: How many of one person's tables may be refused or fail in an hour before they are asked to wait. A file that is wrong still costs a worker time to find out.

settings.name: MUNITAS_TABLE_UPLOAD_PARTS_IN_FLIGHT
settings.meaning: How many parts of one upload may be sent at the same moment. Each part is held in memory while it is stored.

settings.name: MUNITAS_TABLE_UPLOAD_REQUESTS_IN_FLIGHT
settings.meaning: How many parts, across every organisation, the platform will take at the same moment. Past this a part is turned away with a time to wait, so a few large uploads cannot slow everyone else down.

ports.jaeger_otlp_grpc: Where traces are sent over gRPC (the trace store's OTLP receiver).
ports.jaeger_otlp_http: Where traces are sent over HTTP (the trace store's OTLP receiver).
ports.hydra_public: The notebook sign-in service's public interface: the address a person's browser is sent to when a notebook asks to sign in. Its admin interface is not published.
ports.munitas_api_http: The control plane (the API) over plain HTTP.
ports.seaweedfs_s3: Object storage, through its S3 interface.
